steps.phrase: write one ignore pattern per line beside the map
steps.note: The file is committed with the code. A .gitignore cannot say 'tracked, yet not part of what the map describes'.

steps.phrase: hand over the pattern lines in the order they were written
steps.note: The last rule that matches a path is the one that decides it. So a `!` line carves an exception out of a broad ignore. A line whose `#` sits mid-line is one literal pattern, and is reported as unusable.

steps.phrase: ask for the briefing that says what will be read
carry the request to describe the tree, and nothing else
walk the project's files, the same walk the survey and the checks use
ask which rule decides each file the walk found
record which files stayed and how many each rule took out
steps.note: The tally is kept on the walk, not on the parsed file. So one project's counts can never be reported for another.

steps.phrase: ask what each pattern took out, for the briefing
print the file count and every pattern beside what it took out
show the narrowed tree before any code is read
write the per-pattern counts into the code survey beside the map
ask for the map's own checks to run
carry the check request, whether the cheap pass or the full one
walk the tree again instead of trusting the code survey
steps.note: Each coverage check re-measures the repo on its own. The ignore file is the one input both sides read, so it is always disclosed.

steps.phrase: ask what each pattern decided on that second walk
name every pattern that decided nothing on this tree
steps.note: A pattern that took nothing out is a typo, or a tree that moved. Left unsaid it reads as coverage the author never got.

steps.phrase: show what the map was told to leave out, on every check run
ask in plain language to move, split or rename part of the map
point the agent at the clone and at the one document that decides the mode
run the map commands the method names
carry the request to read one element's stored record
read the stored record of the element the person named
carry the request for a proposed split of one crowded screen
print a proposed grouping for a screen that holds too many boxes
show the split as a starting point, never as ready to apply
carry one addressed row rewrite, refusing an address that matches none or many
merge the harvest pieces first, so an edit that would mint or retire an id is refused
steps.note: Rows are merged by their own text. Rewriting that text can split one row in two, or collapse two into one.

steps.phrase: rewrite the named rows in the piece that authored them
steps.note: One write for the whole batch. A later bad edit never leaves the file half changed.

steps.phrase: repoint every use case step that rode an arrow the change removed
note under its own heading the warning the person judged acceptable
name every field that changed, old value then new
show what changed before the checks run

edges.why: builds the walk result saying which files stayed and what each ignore rule decided
reads one element's stored record out of the map
writes the corrected rows back into the stored map
appends a recorded exception under its extras heading
